diagnostics.message: `:resource.aws_lambda_function.main` has a `vpc_config` block driven by `var.lambda.subnet_ids`/`security_group_ids`, but nothing orders it after `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.vpc_execution_role`. When a Lambda function is attached to a VPC, AWS calls CreateNetworkInterface with the execution role at creation time; if `AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole` has not been attached yet, creation fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface on EC2". Add an explicit `depends_on` on the attachment (there is no attribute-level data reference available).

`:resource.aws_lambda_function.main` only references `aws_iam_role.main.arn`, so it can be created before `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging` attaches the CloudWatch Logs permissions to that role. The function's first invocation then fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateLogStream on CloudWatch Logs". The AWS provider's own `aws_lambda_function` docs recommend `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.lambda_logs, aws_cloudwatch_log_group.example]` for exactly this reason. Add an explicit `depends_on` on `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging` (no idiomatic data reference exists, since the function does not consume anything the policy produces).

When `var.lambda.tracing_config.mode` is set, `:resource.aws_lambda_function.main` gets a `tracing_config` block but no ordering against `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.xray`, which grants `xray:PutTraceSegments`/`PutTelemetryRecords`. The function can therefore be created and invoked before the X-Ray permissions exist, so tracing silently fails (and the `Active` mode is rejected at invoke time). Add an explicit `depends_on` from the function to `:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.xray`.
